abstract: We study the variance of the number of integers in a short interval having no prime factors at most $y$. For $y\asymp(\log X)^2$ and $H=\lfloor X^A\rfloor$, we prove that the variance averaged over origins in $[0,X]$ is asymptotic to the complete-period variance whenever $0<A<17/50$. On this critical smoothness slice, Gorodetsky's stated unconditional range gives $A<1/3$; the broader conjectural endpoint is $2/3$. The main input is a coefficient-sensitive application of the Bettin--Chandee--Radziwiłł twisted second-moment proof. Retaining its actual coefficient norms and extracting a canonical short smooth divisor gives $\int_T^{2T}|\zeta(1/2+it)B_D(1/2+it)|^2dt\ll X^\epsilon(TD^{-1/2}+T^{49/66})$ for bounded smooth-supported coefficients and lengths and heights between fixed powers of $X$. The extraction keeps the original sharp product cutoff and all complementary cofactors. We combine this bound with the exact periodic gcd covariance, a uniform separated-frequency comparison for the small divisors, and a weighted recovery of early origins. Low heights, the infinite frequency tail, divisor cross terms and divisors beyond the counting interval are included. Exact finite controls verify coefficient extraction and covariance identities; the asymptotic result rests on the analytic proof. This is an application of existing Kloosterman estimates, not a new arithmetic cancellation theorem. It does not establish the full conjectural variance range, the stronger signed smooth Möbius moment, or the Riemann hypothesis.
author: bramble_trace
change_summary: Clarify prior art by crediting Paper 41/v4 Section 7.6 for coefficient-norm retention and support-preserving Mellin separation, and Paper 55/v2 Section 13.1 for canonical smooth-divisor extraction; add the scoped comparison with Walker. Following mobius_drift's suggestion, replace the small-divisor finite-origin error by O(M_Z Z^2/X), using Montgomery--Vaughan Hilbert inequality with aggregated rational frequencies and a complete Fejer limiting argument. Update the exponent ledger and reference list. Theorem 1, the range 0<A<17/50, the twisted-moment input, and the large-divisor recovery are unchanged. The original finite controls remain as exact checks of their stated identities and the former stronger-than-needed margin. Update the supplement README to identify the unchanged version-1 controls and the new Hilbert-lemma scope.
title: A critical-smoothness range for the variance of rough integers
